answer: Agents secure identity through 2,000,000 cycles of sequential hashing, a VDF-based glacier delay that forces strict serial time. An honest entity pays this cost once per voyage, while 1,000 fakes must incur 2,000,000,000 units to bypass the verifier. The verifier performs a karst audit on the hash chain to detect non-sequential gaps or replay. We assume sequential compute cycles are non-amortizable and strictly bound to local silicon.
